note: Registered cells: each a construction of harness/cells.py applied once to the committed baseline, with the expected outcome of each layer in the reduced form adapter/SPEC.md section 6 defines -- the gateway's ok and its set of finding statuses; the in-toto layer's pass and, per attestation, its first failure (a DSSE code, a statement code, or the subjects that did not match); the binding layer's pass and, per attestation, its code; the combined verdict. Roles: control-gate rows are validity gates evaluated first; endpoint rows decide R1. attackerCapability: none / tamper (bytes changed without any key) / selective-keys (a key that is not the adapter's) / full-keys (the adapter's key). ownership names which layer's own check sees the construction, and which layers are registered undetected.

cells.reason: the corpus vector v3-action-valid verifies under the pinned gateway (both receipts ok, the citation and the record resolve); its two attestations verify under the reference DSSE implementation with the adapter's key, both statements validate, every subject re-digests, and the binding's rules hold

one byte of the action attestation's signature is changed: the reference implementation must refuse it (the check is exercised); the store is untouched, so the gateway sees nothing; the binding compares documents, not signatures

cells.ownership: gateway and in-toto (by re-digest), not the binding
cells.reason: the action's retained response bytes change: the gateway's ladder re-digests the artifact (§1.4 order 8, artifact-mismatch on receipt 1; receipt 0 ok); the in-toto layer's subject re-digest fails for the artifact subject of attestation 1 while its DSSE and statement pass; the binding compares the predicate with the stored receipt, which did not change

cells.ownership: all three, each differently; the acquisition's own attestation is silent
cells.reason: a signed member of the cited acquisition receipt changes in the store: the gateway reports signature-mismatch on receipt 0 (§1.4 order 4) and sequence-broken on the session, receipt 1 itself ok since the citation's signature string is unchanged; the in-toto layer sees it only through the ACTION's attestation, whose cites/s2/0 subject re-digests the cited receipt's file -- the acquisition's own attestation passes, since its subject is the artifact; the binding sees attestation 0's predicate differ from the store

cells.ownership: gateway and in-toto; the binding is silent about an orphaned attestation
cells.reason: the cited receipt is deleted: the gateway's session checks report sequence-broken and tail-rollback (the seal registered two) and step 5 reports citation-unresolved on the action; the in-toto layer's cites/s2/0 subject is missing; the binding, which checks per stored receipt, finds attestation 1 consistent and examines no attestation for a receipt that is gone -- the orphaned attestation 0 is outside its rule

cells.ownership: gateway and in-toto (with the gateway's candidate rule)
cells.reason: the book's line is rewritten: the gateway's step 6 finds no candidate with the claimed digest (decision-record-mismatch); the in-toto layer's decision-record subject finds no candidate either, by the same candidate rule the ceremony adopts from the gateway (a consumer needs that rule to place the subject); the binding is untouched

cells.ownership: gateway only: registered undetected for in-toto and the binding
cells.reason: the seal registry is emptied: the gateway reports the session unregistered (§4 step 3); an attestation has no seal, no session and no count -- the in-toto layer and the binding pass

cells.ownership: all three; the non-gateway layers by the one-attestation-per-receipt rule
cells.reason: a copy of the action receipt is appended at index 2: the gateway reports it misfiled (its callIndex says 1) and the session's count over the seal; the in-toto and binding layers, which expect one attestation per stored receipt, report the third receipt's attestation missing -- they see the appended receipt only because the ceremony requires an attestation per receipt, not because they read the seal

cells.ownership: gateway and the binding; registered undetected for in-toto
cells.reason: a signed member of the action receipt (decision.packDigest) changes in the store while the attestation keeps the original: the gateway reports signature-mismatch on receipt 1; the in-toto layer passes -- the envelope is self-consistent and its subjects still re-digest; only the binding, comparing the predicate with the stored receipt, sees the difference

cells.ownership: in-toto and the binding; the gateway cannot see attestations
cells.reason: the attestation's payload is altered (the predicate's authority) without re-signing: the reference implementation refuses the signature; the binding, reading the altered payload, finds the predicate differs from the store; the gateway reads no attestation and reports ok

the action's attestation is rebuilt and signed with a key that is not the adapter's: its signature's key id is not the pinned one (untrusted-key); the binding, which verifies no signature, finds the statement consistent; the gateway sees nothing

cells.ownership: the binding only: registered undetected for in-toto and the gateway
cells.structure: attestation tampering with the adapter's key, store untouched
cells.reason: holding the adapter's key, the action's artifact subject is pointed at the acquisition's artifact and the statement re-signed: the reference implementation verifies the envelope, the statement validates, and the subject re-digests -- that artifact exists in the store -- so the in-toto layer passes; only the binding, which holds the artifact subject to the predicate's resultDigest, sees it; the gateway sees nothing. This is the binding's sharpest limit: a valid attestation vouching for the wrong artifact

cells.structure: attestation tampering with the adapter's key, store untouched
cells.reason: the predicate type is changed and the statement re-signed: the ceremony pins the registered predicate type (a consumer that did not would pass); the binding checks subjects against the predicate, which is unchanged

cells.structure: attestation tampering with the adapter's key, store untouched
cells.reason: the statement's _type is changed to an older Statement version and re-signed: the ceremony pins Statement v1
the action's attestation is deleted: both non-gateway layers require one attestation per stored receipt; the gateway sees nothing
the envelope's payloadType is changed: the ceremony holds it to the in-toto type before verifying (the PAE would differ anyway); the binding still reads a consistent statement

cells.ownership: the binding only: registered undetected for in-toto and the gateway
cells.structure: attestation tampering with the adapter's key, store untouched
cells.reason: holding the adapter's key, the predicate's copy of the action receipt is altered (decision.packDigest) and re-signed: the envelope verifies, the statement validates, every subject still re-digests -- the in-toto layer passes; the binding compares the predicate with the stored receipt and sees the difference; the gateway sees nothing

cells.structure: attestation tampering with the adapter's key, store untouched
cells.reason: holding the adapter's key, the action's cited-receipt subject is removed and the statement re-signed: a statement with fewer subjects is still a valid, verifying statement to the in-toto layer; the binding requires one cites subject per citation in the predicate

cells.ownership: gateway only: registered undetected for in-toto and the binding
cells.structure: a store under another gateway key, bound afresh
cells.reason: both receipts are re-signed under another Ed25519 key with its own keyId and the attestations bound afresh by the adapter: the gateway, verifying under the corpus key, reports key-mismatch on both (§1.4 order 3); the attestations verify under the adapter's key and every subject re-digests; the binding holds. The binding carries no trust in the gateway's key: an in-toto consumer cannot tell this store from the genuine one
